Subject: Request: Vector latency benchmarking runbook and onramp

Hi Priyom / Ben —

Thanks again for the intro earlier. VectorWorks is prepping an evaluation for a customer that needs consistent p99 latency below 120ms for 512-dim embeddings across a 1M-vector index. They want a short technical runbook we can follow to reproduce Redwood + Pinecone/Weaviate + S3 fallthrough latency numbers in our environment so their infra team can sign off.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a step-by-step benchmark plan (data ingestion, index build, query pattern, measuring p50/p95/p99, network conditions to emulate) and a short onramp checklist for SREs (VPC peering, egress, tuning knobs we should test — batching, prefetch, cache warmup)?

We can run the test harness on our side if you provide the runbook + a template CSV/JSONL for queries. Timeline: can we get a draft by EOD next Tue (2027-07-20)? The customer review is the week after.

Attachments: sample-corpus-10k.jsonl (example queries)

Thanks,
Emma Caldwell

VectorWorks Consulting
emma@vectorworks.ai

Emma — appreciate the clear ask. We're happy to produce a reproducible runbook. Initial plan below; Ben and Lauren will own technical validation and the deliverables.

Quick plan (draft):
- Deliverable 1: "Vector Latency Runbook" (markdown) — steps for environment setup, ingestion, index build, warmup, query profiles, measurement scripts.
- Deliverable 2: Bench template (Excel) — p50/p95/p99, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, egress stats.
- Deliverable 3: Short SRE onramp checklist — VPC peering, allowed ports, IAM roles, recommended replica counts + fallback policy for S3 cold tier.

We need answers to a couple of constraints to tune the run:
1) Query QPS target during test (sustained and spike) — default suggest 10 qps sustained, 50 qps spike.
2) Average query size / tokens we should model for read path.
3) Do you want to include rerank stage (LLM call) as part of the end-to-end test or separate?

We will produce a first draft by COB Monday (2027-07-19) so you have time to validate before your Tue target. Attaching a skeleton runbook and the bench template (vector-latency-runbook-draft.md, prelim-bench-template.xlsx).

Regards,

Emma / team — adding technical detail we'll include in the runbook and things I want VectorWorks to try in your preliminary run: 

Bench assumptions & knobs to capture:
- Index types: Pinecone (dense vector, 1M vectors, nprobe/hnsw degree) and Weaviate (HNSW parameters). We'll record indexing time and memory.
- Replica topology: 1 vs 3 replicas, measure cold vs warm p99.
- Embedding vector size: 512-dim baseline; we'll include tests at 256/1024 to show sensitivity.
- Batching: client-side batch size for multi-query (1, 8, 32) and server batching where supported.
- KV/prefix caching: measure response delta with Redwood prefix cache warm vs empty KV.
- S3 fallthrough: simulate a miss path where top-K comes from cold S3 fallback (RDS + pgvector or S3 object store with a small cache) — we'll measure cost/latency delta.
- Network emulation: 10ms, 30ms, 80ms added RTT scenarios (to simulate cross-region).

Data/workflow details:
- Ingest pipeline should use the sample-corpus-10k.jsonl you attached; we will provide a script to bulk load into Pinecone/Weaviate and into a pgvector test DB.
- Query mix: 70% single-vector topK(5), 20% multi-vector batch, 10% complex rerank (if enabled).

Instrumentation we will provide:
- Scripted harness (Python) to drive queries and collect token-level traces from Redwood: per-request latency, token counts, kernel times, and egress bytes.
- Excel template for metrics + Grafana dashboard pointers.

I'll attach the initial template and a short sample CSV for you to run (prelim-bench-template.xlsx). If VectorWorks can run an initial 1-hour baseline with the sample corpus, we can iterate.

—Ben
